title: Barry Switzer's Career Record at Oklahoma: 157-29-4 and .837
question: What was Barry Switzer's career record and winning percentage at Oklahoma?
answer: Barry Switzer went 157-29-4 in 16 seasons as Oklahoma's head coach (1973-1988), an .837 winning percentage, with 12 Big Eight titles and three national championships. His 157 wins were the school record until Bob Stoops passed him in 2013.
summary: Barry Switzer went 157-29-4 (.837) in 16 seasons at OU from 1973 to 1988, winning 12 Big Eight titles. Here are the numbers behind his record.
body: Barry Switzer's numbers at Oklahoma hold up against anyone's. Named head coach on Jan. 29, 1973, after Chuck Fairbanks left for the NFL, he ran the program for 16 seasons through 1988 and finished 157-29-4. That works out to an .837 winning percentage, which the College Football Hall of Fame says ranked fourth all-time among major-college coaches when he retired.

The Arkansas native, born in Crossett in 1937, had played linebacker for the Razorbacks and coached there before joining OU's staff in 1966. As a head coach he won 12 Big Eight championships in his 16 years and three national titles. His teams went 8-5 in 13 bowl games, and OU's 37-game unbeaten streak from 1972 to 1975 came mostly on his watch, with 30 of those games after he took over.

The scoreboard tells the story of his wishbone attack. Over his tenure, Oklahoma outscored opponents 6,093 to 2,429, roughly 32 points per game to 13. From 1973 through 1980 alone, OU went 83-9-2 running the wishbone, and the Sooners' 102 wins in the 1970s were the most of any Division I program.

Switzer's 157 victories stood as the OU record until Bob Stoops passed him in November 2013. He later coached the Dallas Cowboys to a Super Bowl XXX win, and the College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 2001.
